Deduction.zeroFree_of_rpow_window.title: The positive weights in the family
Deduction.zeroFree_of_rpow_window.reading_note: `CharFamily` asks for positive weights on the characters, not positive prime-power coefficients or positive values of $G_F$. Its members are non-principal characters or the character of modulus one, for which the zeta correction is used instead. On the window take the non-negative majorant $R(y)=|C|y^\theta$; then $\int_Y^{Y^{1+\omega}}R(y)y^{-\theta-1}\,dy=|C|\omega\log Y\le Y^\eta$ for any fixed $\eta>0$ and sufficiently large $Y$. This is `windowHyp_of_rpow`; under $v=\log y$, $U=\log Y$, the integral becomes $\int_U^{(1+\omega)U}R(e^v)e^{-\theta v}\,dv\le e^{\eta U}$, the bound used in `lemmaL`.

Deduction.landau_window.title: The two cases of the pole argument
Deduction.landau_window.reading_note: Let $D$ be the distance from $\sigma$ to the nearest pole, truncated at $\sigma-\theta$. If some pole has horizontal distance $\sigma-\operatorname{Re}\rho<D$, move the centre to near its height; by avoiding ties one obtains a unique nearest pole at distance $d<D$, whereas the disc of radius $D$ at $\sigma$ contains no pole. If there is no such pole, the assumed pole to the right of $\theta$ implies $D<\sigma-\theta$, and a nearest pole must be the real point $\beta=\sigma-D$: otherwise its horizontal distance would be less than $D$. In the first case the real-centre Taylor term is of smaller order than the shifted pole term; in the second case the residue is positive and no shift is needed.

Deduction.landau_window.title: Why the argument is windowed
Deduction.landau_window.reading_note: On the logarithmic window $[U,(1+\omega)U]$, $U=\log Y$, choose $k=\lceil(1+\omega/2)\sigma U\rceil$ so the kernel $w_k(v)=v^ke^{-\sigma v}/k!$ peaks near the middle, at $v=k/\sigma$. What is needed outside this window is not merely small kernel mass: the preliminary bound for $|G_F(e^v)|$ is $C_0e^{2v}$, and `landau_tails` chooses $\sigma$ large in terms of $\omega$ so that the integral of $e^{2v}w_k(v)$ off the window is $O(\sigma^{-k})$. On the window the exponential series gives $w_k(v)\le e^{-\theta v}(\sigma-\theta)^{-k}$, so the integral against the majorant costs at most $e^{\eta U}(\sigma-\theta)^{-k}$. The same order $k\ge U$ works at every height, and later windows provide arbitrarily large such orders.

Formalism.HN.TheoremF.title: Theorem F and its sharper form
Formalism.HN.TheoremF.reading_note: If $c(\tau)$ is the fraction of the slopes of $P$ strictly below $\bar\mu-\tau$ (counted with rank multiplicity), each slope $\lambda$ contributes to $\int_0^{HH}c(\tau)\,d\tau$ for an interval of length $(\bar\mu-\lambda)_+$, since $\mu_{\min}(P)\ge\bar\mu-HH$. The integral is thus the mean of the positive deficits, which is at least $\bar\mu-\mu(P)$. The rank estimate bounds $c(\tau)$ by $\min(1,w(\tau))$, where $w(\tau)=(1-\delta_F)^{-1}(\eta_F+4\sqrt{e_F}+4u_F/(u_F+\tau))$, the quotient being zero for $u_F=0$. The cap is useful near $\tau=0$; `layer_cake_formula` uses it, and the proof then bounds its integral by $\int_0^{HH}w(\tau)\,d\tau$, giving the two terms in parentheses in line 62. This already proves `TheoremFSharp` under the same hypotheses; `theoremF_of_sharp` weakens it by subtracting $\log|I|\ge0$, using only the nonemptiness of $I$. No part of the filtration or frame argument produces that term. This is the form of (Slope) used in [Section 5.2](pdf#subsection.5.2).

Formalism.LFunctionChainParameters.Weigh.title: Where the two main terms agree
Formalism.LFunctionChainParameters.Weigh.reading_note: `SDiv` is the sum $m\sum_t(\operatorname{ph}(a_t)-a_t\log\Omega)$, `sumA` is $\sum_t a_t$, and `Lam5` is the numerical lower-bound expression in `Count5`, not the actual $\log T(u)$. The lemma needs only $v>0$, $f>0$ and positive weights at the chosen translate: it invokes the earlier `key_identity` and unfolds the changed level expression, without using the inequalities of `Count5`. Its use in `Ga_bound5` is to identify `K5v5` with `Main u0 + K0v5`, separating the exact main term from the counting, divisor, exponent and source-slope errors. The actual level is compared with `Lam5` earlier, in `s_lower5`.

UpperTheory.Top.VVle.title: Why finiteness is a separate conjunct
UpperTheory.Top.VVle.reading_note: In `VVle` the first conjunct excludes infinite length separately for every prime and every $1\le e<t$. This must precede the numerical inequality: `shaLen` takes values in $\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ and `toNat` would otherwise send $\infty$ to zero. The lemma `VVle.mono` also shows that a bound for a larger twist cutoff can be used for a smaller one, by nonnegativity of the lengths; no equality of the two cutoffs is required.

GlobalTheory.IndefiniteRowSideFullHecke..title: The fraction-field splitting and the length convention
GlobalTheory.IndefiniteRowSideFullHecke..reading_note: `IsRankRPart` gives the splitting $r_\pi\otimes K\simeq\rho\oplus\bigoplus_{c=1}^{t}\chi_c$ over $K=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal O)$, where $t$ is the block width `R.t`; the integral representation need not split. The Selmer group in `sPi` has coefficients $(K/\mathcal O)^r$ with action $\rho\otimes\chi_1^{-1}$. The lengths of torsion modules over $\mathcal O$ are divided by $\operatorname{len}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal O/\ell\mathcal O)$, so the valuation is normalised by $v_\ell(\ell)=1$. In particular for a finite $\mathcal O$-module $A$, this normalised length is $\operatorname{len}_{\mathbb Z_\ell}(A)/[K:\mathbb Q_\ell]$: expanding a twisted $K/\mathcal O$ coefficient using a $\mathbb Z_\ell$-basis of $\mathcal O$ introduces no field-degree factor in the final normalised bound. `CongBound_at` is the bound as a predicate, with matching weights, a good lift, and a Hecke-compatible Galois family at every eigensystem as additional hypotheses.

UpperTheory.Top.supplyChi.title: The uniform rank-existence input to host supply
UpperTheory.Top.supplyChi.reading_note: The result of `supplyChi` concerns a host carrying the rank and level data, not just a cyclotomic field with the correct ramification. In `supplyOfAdm` the remaining hypothesis is that for every preliminary field datum of the prescribed sizes there are ranks with `RankVal` and `admitted`; the latter says that the preliminary datum can be extended to a host for every choice of the indicated level data. The theorem `admissibleClassesTwistedChar` supplies this with a lower bound on $x$ independent of the preliminary field. The proof of `supplyChi` substitutes the equality of the two $\varepsilon$ parameters and applies that theorem, leaving the prime selection and the host construction to `supplyOfAdm`.

UpperTheory.Top.PairEx.title: Why the second prime has the larger search range
UpperTheory.Top.PairEx.reading_note: First choose $q$ in the progression $3\pmod8$, good for all the required $q$-twists. With $q$ fixed, the $d$-choice must treat both the original base characters and their $q$-twists, so as to supply the two remaining nontrivial choices of $(i,j)$. Put $z=Y^{\varepsilon/5}$; the progression now has modulus $16q\prod_{3\le p\le z,\ p\ \mathrm{prime}}p$ and is $7$ modulo $16$ and $-1$ at the odd factors, a reduced residue class. Its modulus has logarithm $O(z)$, and the upper endpoint $U=\exp(z(\log Y)^2)$ has $\log U=z(\log Y)^2$, leaving room for the prime number theorem in progressions used here, whose size condition is $\log U\ge C_0\log M\log\log M$ for progression modulus $M$. The counting argument leaves at least half of the first family, and at least half of the second family for each good first prime; this gives a single pair good throughout the window, not two independently selected primes.

Formalism.MainNotions.LocalQuadraticPart.title: The exact integrality statement
Formalism.MainNotions.LocalQuadraticPart.reading_note: For a word $u$ and place $w$, the form ranges over `L.NuLat u`, and $F$ ranges over the integral test vectors in `Mtilde (muAt w)` that also lie in `V0 (muAt w)`. The existential $y$ first identifies the complex column period with an element of the coefficient field; it is this element whose valuation is taken. Here `sg` is $g(u,w)$ and `ur` multiplies it by the ramification index, so the bound on a nonzero $y$ is precisely $v_w(y)\ge\lfloor e_w g(u,w)\rfloor$. The next lemma uses $\lfloor r\rfloor\le r$ to pass from the unrounded valuation bound to this predicate.

Formalism.HN.frameB_share.title: How the cut rank is bounded
Formalism.HN.frameB_share.reading_note: The variables `x i j` are real numbers, not lattice vectors, and `m i` counts entries with multiplicity. To apply the lemma to the lattice, put $n_K=[K:\mathbb Q]$ and $c_K=-\log2+\log|d_K|/n_K$ as in [Section 5.1](pdf#subsection.5.1). For an entry $\lambda_{ij}$ of the unnormalised `slopeList` of the underlying $\mathbb Z$-lattice, use $x_{ij}=2\lambda_{ij}+c_K-h_i$; the threshold passed to `hnStep` is therefore $(s-\tau+h_i-c_K)/2$. By `frameB_count_lt`, the number of entries strictly below this threshold is the difference of the $\mathbb Z$-ranks of the original and retained lattices. Each is $n_K$ times its $K$-rank, so the bound for the fraction lost is unchanged.

UpperTheory.Top.divinN_of_hypV.title: The three premises supplied by the cohomological bound
UpperTheory.Top.divinN_of_hypV.reading_note: The threshold is the maximum of those for `HypV`, `LinkN`, equality of the ranks $d_j=D_0$, the inequality $(\log x)^2\le x^\varepsilon$ and the scale identities. From `vvRecord` the first component (finiteness) is used to specialise `LinkN`, the second (summability) to apply its local inequality, and the third to bound the series by $\sqrt b\le b$. The last line uses the family scale identities to apply the logarithmic inequality at the common $x$. This gives one constant $|C|+1$ for all members of the family and all lifts above the threshold.

Formalism.LFunctionChainParameters.LChai.title: The eleven conditions on the numerical data
Formalism.LFunctionChainParameters.LChai.reading_note: There are two declarations with the short name `SizeData₂`. The one in `BasicNotions` records the arithmetic data used to define the rescaled lattice; the one here in `LChain` is a conjunction of inequalities on numerical data `Dd`. In `TieLocal` the ranks, slopes, level primes, height bounds and finite-place sums of `Dd` are identified with those of the constructed lattices; `each_unit_bound_statement` needs only the eleven numerical hypotheses and gives $\mathrm{ASK}(u_0)\le\mathrm{MAIN}(u_0)+\mathrm{ErrX5at}(u_0)$ for each $u_0$. The identification with the analytic count and the bound on this explicit error are further conditions of the application.

Formalism.MainNotions.LocalQuadraticPart.title: A worked example of the divisibility compensation

reader_notes.Deduction.landau_window: Put $T_k(s)=(-1)^k\Phi^{(k)}(s)/k!$ and $E=\sigma-\theta$. A pole of residue $c$ at $\rho$ contributes $c/(s-\rho)^{k+1}$ to this coefficient. In the shifted-centre case one bounds the real-centre coefficient and the shifted holomorphic remainder by Cauchy's estimate; in the real-pole case the positive residue gives a lower bound for $\operatorname{Re}T_k(\sigma)$ directly. Thus the estimate of `landau_window_key` in either case would imply $a/d^k\le M/r'^k+Ae^{\eta U}/E^k$, where $a>0$, $d$ is the distance to the isolated pole and $d<r'\le E$. After multiplication by $d^k$, the right side tends to zero for $0<\eta<\log(r'/d)$, since $U\le k$ and $k$ can be arbitrarily large; the left side is the fixed number $a$.
